name: Starr
description: Web UI for diagnosing and repairing the SQLite databases used by Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Sportarr, Readarr, Prowlarr, Whisparr, and Bazarr. Safely stops the target *arr container, takes a (zstd-compressed) timestamped backup, runs SQLite PRAGMA repairs (integrity check, FK repair, WAL checkpoint, VACUUM, REINDEX, ANALYZE) on the idle database, then starts the container back up. Repair output streams live to the browser via SSE — scheduled runs stream into the same log. Features: cron scheduler with skip-if-clean, multiple instances per app (e.g. a second Sonarr), run history with last-run pill + pre-repair time estimate + per-instance trend charts, one-click restore from any backup, mid-VACUUM cancel (real SQLite interrupt), per-instance backup retention up to 1 year, and notifications on completion via Apprise (Discord/Telegram/ntfy/Pushover/…), Signal (signal-cli-rest-api), or plain JSON webhooks. With the Docker socket mounted and a single /appdata mount pointed at your host appdata root, Starr auto-discovers each *arr container — its URL, container name, and database path — so you only need to paste the API keys and click Save Credentials. Provided as-is, no warranty — reliable in our testing, but use at your own risk and keep your own backups. The authors aren't responsible for any data loss or database damage.

paths.name: Appdata root
paths.description: Host appdata root (contains each *arr's config folder). Starr uses Docker introspection to find each *arr's /config inside this single mount, so you don't need a separate mount per app. Read-write is required because VACUUM/REINDEX/FK repair write to the source database.

paths.name: Backups
paths.description: Where timestamped database backups are stored. Backups are auto-pruned based on MAX_BACKUP_AGE_DAYS.

paths.name: Docker Socket (optional)
paths.description: OPTIONAL, but recommended on Unraid. Mounting the host Docker socket lets Starr auto-discover your *arr containers and stop/start them around a repair — more reliable than the app's shutdown API when a container restart policy is in play. NOTE: the Docker socket grants root-equivalent control of the host Docker daemon (the same trade-off as Portainer/Watchtower/Dockge). If you'd rather not grant that, clear this field: Starr falls back to each app's HTTP shutdown API and you enter URLs/API keys manually.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: Port for the Starr web dashboard.

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: UID the container runs as. Must own — or share a group with — the *arr config dirs under your appdata root so VACUUM/REINDEX can write the source DB. Unraid default: 99 (nobody).

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: GID the container runs as. Unraid default: 100 (users).

variables.name: SECRET_KEY
variables.description: REQUIRED. Web UI access key (your 'Web Key' at the login gate). Set a strong random value — e.g. run: openssl rand -hex 32. If left blank / at the built-in default, Starr runs UNAUTHENTICATED: anyone who can reach the port gets in, and the dashboard shows an 'insecure' banner. Always set this on a shared network.

variables.name: LOG_LEVEL
variables.description: Log verbosity: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR.

variables.name: MAX_BACKUP_AGE_DAYS
variables.description: Number of days to keep backups before auto-pruning. Set to 0 to disable pruning.

variables.name: SONARR_APIKEY
variables.description: Sonarr API key (Settings › General › API Key). Leave blank to disable.

variables.name: RADARR_APIKEY
variables.description: Radarr API key. Leave blank to disable.
